summary: Shows a rolling update with serial: 5 that removes each host from the load balancer in pre_tasks, applies roles, flushes handlers, runs a testing role, and only re-adds the host if tests pass; max_fail_percentage can stop the rollout.
questions: How do I only put a server back in the load balancer if its tests pass?
How do I do a rolling deploy with health checks in Ansible?
How can I stop a rolling update if too many hosts fail?
How do I run handlers before my test tasks?

answer_card.title: Gate rolling updates with tests
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
- hosts: webservers
  serial: 5
  pre_tasks:
    - name: take out of load balancer pool
      ansible.builtin.command: /usr/bin/take_out_of_pool {{ inventory_hostname }}
      delegate_to: 127.0.0.1
  tasks:
    - ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: "{{ item }}"
      loop: [common, webserver]
    - ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
    - ansible.builtin.include_role:
        name: apply_testing_checks
  post_tasks:
    - name: add back to load balancer pool
      ansible.builtin.command: /usr/bin/add_back_to_pool {{ inventory_hostname }}
      delegate_to: 127.0.0.1
```

If the tests fail, the host never returns to the pool. Use `max_fail_percentage` to stop the rollout after too many failures.
